t: You're standing in Smith Square, just south of the Palace of Westminster. Most of the garden in the middle is taken up by St John's, a Baroque church that's now a concert hall. The buildings around it are mostly offices, home to organisations that lobby or serve the government. In the middle of the last century, the headquarters of Britain's two biggest political parties were here. The band leader and entertainer Billy Cotton was born on this square. The architect and politician Alfred Bossom died here.
